name: Medora de Morès
role: Wife of the Marquis de Morès; builder of Medora's Catholic church
bio: The Marquise de Morès, wife of the Marquis, arrived in Medora in April 1884 in the Marquis' private car and came and went with him through 1886. In September 1884 the corner-stone was laid for a Catholic church she was building in the town, which Father Martin blessed that November; Catholic residents publicly thanked her, and she offered the church as a school house. The paper announced the birth of her son in March 1885, and that June she started the machinery of the new abattoir. In summer 1885 she went on a hunting trip to the Big Horn country, where the paper credited her with killing several bears, and she made more hunting trips down the river in 1885 and 1886, including one with the Marquis in October 1886 that took mountain sheep, elk and antelope. In October 1885 she renewed her offer to pay a teacher's salary if the school board would open a school.
